title: Supreme Court: 27-Year Sales Tax Surcharge Reference Has Turned Academic After GST
case_name: Arjun Flour Mills v. State of Odisha (with the connected reference in S. Kodar v. State of Kerala)
citation: Civil Appeal No. 8763 of 1994; 2026 INSC 1192, decided 4 November 2026
card_summary: A seven-judge Constitution Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant disposed of a reference pending since 1999 on whether a state can impose a surcharge calculated on sales tax, arising from Section 5A of the Orissa Sales Tax Act, 1947. The Bench held the question had turned academic once GST replaced the pre-GST sales tax framework, and that S. Kodar v. State of Kerala continues to hold the field.
card_tip: A business still contesting an old, pre-GST additional sales tax or surcharge demand should expect courts to treat Kodar as settled law on the State's power to levy it, rather than reopen that question.
verification_notes: The case name, the 1999 reference, the challenge under Section 5A of the Orissa Sales Tax Act, the seven-judge bench headed by CJI Surya Kant, the 4 November 2026 decision date, the 'academic'/infructuous finding and the continued reliance on S. Kodar are consistent across Verdictum, LiveLaw, SC Observer, LawStreet and LawChakra reports seen in this run. The citation 2026 INSC 1192 and the open question on the Punjab General Sales Tax Act, 1948 surcharge are reported by LawStreet; the full bench composition beyond the Chief Justice was seen only in LawStreet and LawChakra. The judgment text itself was not opened in this run.
